source_text: ’Εκ πλείστου ὅσου καὶ ἱκανωτάτου χρόνου, ἀγαπητὲ Ἀουίρκιε Μάρκελλε, ἐπιταχθεὶς ὑπὸ σοῦ συγγράψαι τινὰ λόγον εἰς τὴν τῶν κατὰ Μιλτιάδην λεγομένων αἵρεσιν, ἐφεκτικώτερόν πως μέχρι νῦν διεκείμην· οὐκ ἀπορίᾳ τοῦ δύνασθαι ἐλέγχειν μὲν τὸ ψεῦδος, μαρτυρεῖν δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ· δεδιὼς δὲ καὶ ἐξευλαβούμενος, μή πῃ δόξω τισὶν ἐπισυγγράφειν ἢ ἐπιδιατάσσεσθαι τῷ τῆς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καινῆς διαθήκης λόγῳ· ᾧ μήτε προσθεῖναι μήτ’ ἀφελεῖν δυνατὸν, τῷ κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον αὐτὸ πολιτεύεσθαι προῃρημένῳ. προσφάτως δὲ γενόμενος ἐν Ἀγκύρᾳ τῆς Γαλατίας· καὶ καταλαβὼν τὴν κατὰ τόπον ἐκκλησίαν ὑπὸ τῆς νέας ταύτης οὐχ ὡς αὐτοὶ φασὶ προφητείας· πολὺ δὲ μᾶλλον ὡς δειχθήσεται ψευδοπροφητείας διατεθρυλλημένην, καθόσον δυνατὸν, τοῦ Κυρίου παρασχόντος, περὶ αὐτῶν τε τούτων καὶ τῶν προτεινομένων ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἑκάστοτε διελέχθημεν ἡμέραις πλείοσιν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ· ὡς τὴν μὲν ἐκκλησίαν ἀγαλλιασθῆναι, καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐπιῤῥωσθῆναι· τοὺς δὲ ἐξεναντίας πρὸς τὸ παρὸν ἀποκρουσθῆναι· καὶ τοὺς ἀντιθέτους λυπηθῆναι. ἀξιούντων οὖν τῶν κατὰ τόπον πρεσβυτέρων, ὅπως τῶν λεχθέντων κατὰ τῶν ἀντιδιατιθεμένων τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγῳ ὑπόμνημά τι καταλίπωμεν· παρόντος καὶ τοῦ συμπρεσβυτέρου ἡμῶν Ζωτικοῦ τοῦ Ὀτρηνοῦ, τοῦτο μὲν οὐκ ἐπράξαμεν· ἐπηγγειλάμεθα δὲ ἐνθάδε γράψαντες τοῦ Κυρίου διδόντος, διὰ σπουδῆς πέμψειν αὐτοῖς.
thought_title: Why the author delayed writing against the new prophecy
orientation: The author addresses Avircius Marcellus, explaining why he has only now written the treatise against the Cataphrygian heresy that Avircius commissioned.
pass_a_gloss: For a very long and quite sufficient time, beloved Avircius Marcellus, having been commanded by you to write some discourse against the heresy of those called followers of Miltiades, I was disposed somewhat more hesitantly until now; not from lack of ability to refute the falsehood and to bear witness to the truth; but fearing and being cautious, lest somehow I should seem to some to write in addition to or to make further ordinances for the word of the new covenant of the gospel; to which it is not possible to add or to take away, for the one who has chosen to conduct his life according to the gospel itself. But recently, having been in Ancyra of Galatia, and having found the church in that place thoroughly agitated by this new thing, not as they themselves say prophecy, but much rather, as will be shown, false prophecy, as far as possible, the Lord granting it, we discussed both these very matters and the things proposed by them on each occasion for several days in the church; so that the church rejoiced and was strengthened toward the truth; and those of the opposing side were for the present repulsed; and the adversaries were grieved. Therefore, since the elders of that place were requesting that we leave behind some memorandum of the things said against those who oppose the word of truth, our fellow elder Zoticus of Otrenus also being present, this we did not do; but we promised, writing here, the Lord granting it, to send it to them with diligence.

choices.english: the heresy of those called followers of Miltiades
choices.why: The source says 'those called according to Miltiades'; rendering as 'followers of Miltiades' preserves the sense that the group is named after Miltiades while keeping the passive 'called' explicit.
The comparative adverb with πως conveys a degree of hesitation or reserve; 'hesitantly' captures the author's cautious delay without implying outright refusal.

choices.english: to write in addition to or to make further ordinances for
choices.why: Both verbs carry the prefix ἐπι- indicating addition; the first concerns adding written content, the second concerns adding authoritative rulings, matching the author's fear of seeming to supplement the gospel.
rejected: to append or to legislate further
to add to or to prescribe for

choices.why: The perfect passive participle of διαθρυλέω means 'to be much talked about' or 'thoroughly disturbed'; 'thoroughly agitated' conveys the disruptive effect of the new prophecy on the church.
ὑπόμνημα is a written record or memorandum; the indefinite τι is preserved as 'some' to match the source's tentativeness.
The genitive absolute expresses condition or circumstance; rendering as a participial phrase keeps the source's dependence on divine permission explicit.

bible_refs.note: μήτε προσθεῖναι μήτ' ἀφελεῖν echoes the warning not to add to or take away from the words of the prophecy, though the author applies it to the gospel covenant.

pass_b_english: For a very long and considerable time, beloved Avircius Marcellus, I held back somewhat, even though you had commanded me to write a discourse against the heresy of those called followers of Miltiades. It was not that I lacked the ability to refute the lie and bear witness to the truth. Rather, I was afraid and cautious that I might seem to some people to be adding to or taking away from the word of the new covenant of the gospel. No one who has chosen to conduct his life according to the gospel may add to that word or take away from it. But recently I was in Ancyra in Galatia, and I found the church there much disturbed by rumor of this new prophecy. It is not, as they themselves say, prophecy, but much more, as will be shown, false prophecy. So, as far as possible, with the Lord granting it, we discussed these very matters and the arguments they put forward on each occasion for several days in the church. As a result, the church rejoiced and was strengthened toward the truth, while those on the opposing side were repulsed for the present and the adversaries were grieved. The local elders then asked that we leave behind some memorandum of what had been said against those who oppose the word of truth, and our fellow elder Zoticus of Otrenus was present as well. This we did not do, but we promised to write and, with the Lord granting it, to send it to them with diligence.

problems.ruling: Greek ἐπράξαμεν is plural “we did”; translation renders singular “I did”, changing agency.
